subject: history
title: What the Indus people ate, wore and wrote

scenes.narration: A number of crops were cultivated: cereals like wheat and barley, pulses, oilseeds like mustard and sesame, and millets like bajra, ragi and jowar. Fish, meat, milk, date and fruit were also eaten.

nodes: Cotton thread spun on clay spindles
Long, flowing cloth, skirts and shawls
props.label: Clothes, p.30

scenes.narration: Spindles made of clay were found in many sites; spindles are used to spin cotton thread. Men wore long, flowing cloth, women may have worn skirts, and both draped a shawl over their shoulders.

nodes: Seals of baked clay or steatite
Written from the right to the left
props.label: The Indus script, p.30

scenes.narration: They wrote in one of the world’s earliest known scripts, seen on seals. The writing was mainly brief inscriptions, written from the right to the left. Historians are still trying to decipher it.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a millet?
questions.explanation: Millets like bajra, ragi and jowar (p.29).

questions.prompt: The Indus script was written from the left to the right.
questions.explanation: It was written from the right to the left (p.30).
